content:
We need to find template that when applied to given molecule (initial_molecule) reproduces the carbonyl-ene reaction retrosynthesis. The initial molecule is given with atom mapping: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

We need to find a template that matches this molecule and corresponds to carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular). The tool to search templates requires valid SMILES. Our SMILES should be without mapping. Let's convert to SMILES: CH2=C(Cc1ccccc1)C1CCC[C1](O)C(F)(F)F? Wait mapping: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

So central carbon 2 attached to aromatic ring (c3) and to chiral carbon 9. So SMILES: C=C(Cc1ccccc1)C1CCC[C1](O)C(F)(F)F? plus maybe stereochemistry. So we can use "C=C(Cc1ccccc1)C1CCC[C1](O)C(F)(F)F". Let's try search with functional groups broken: ketones (but we have no ketone? Actually carbonyl-ene reaction consumes a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene to form new C-C and C-O. In product we have a carbonyl? Wait initial molecule is product of carbonyl-ene? The description says forward reaction: alkene + carbonyl -> new C-C bond, new hydroxyl, etc. So retrosynthesis: we need to break product into alkene and carbonyl fragments. So the template should break a C-O bond (hydroxyl) and a C-C bond? Actually carbonyl-ene: product has hydroxyl and new C-C bond, original carbonyl becomes alcohol? The carbonyl is reduced to alcohol? In ene reaction, carbonyl acts as electrophile, forming new C-C bond and moving double bond. The product is an allylic alcohol. So the template likely breaks a C-O bond (the OH) and a C-C bond (new bond) and forms a C=O and C=C. So functional groups broken: aliphatic hydroxyls, five-membered rings? Wait five-membered ring formed in product (maybe cyclopentane). Indeed product has a cyclopentane ring (C1CCC[C1]) attached to carbonyl carbon? Actually product includes a cyclopentane ring fused? The product has a five-membered ring (C1CCC[C1]) attached to carbon bearing OH and CF3. So in retrosynthesis, we break that ring? The description says five-membered rings are formed in product, so broken groups are not five-membered rings. So functional groups broken: ketones, C-C double bonds. Formed: aliphatic hydroxyls, five-membered rings. That's what we attempted.

But search tool expects valid SMILES; our SMILES maybe correct. Let's test with check_smiles_reaction_template_matching after we find template. But first need to get templates. Maybe we can search without functional groups but with bonds broken/formed. However we need correct bond format: "6-6" etc. Not sure.

Alternative: maybe we can directly retrieve a known template ID for carbonyl-ene reaction. Could guess? Not reliable.

Maybe we can use get_template to list? No.

We could try search with functional groups only: functional_groups_broken ["ketones"], functional_groups_formed ["aliphatic hydroxyls","five-membered rings"].

Let's try.
